claims.text: Elevated-temperature degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 is governed by surface-oxidation kinetics.
An oxidizing atmosphere produces a continuous Cr-rich oxide scale.
The continuous Cr-rich oxide scale protects the underlying microstructure.
Limited oxygen in a reducing atmosphere prevents complete surface passivation.
Reducing conditions promote internal oxidation through formation of Ti-rich oxide precipitates.
The starting additively manufactured alloy has a homogeneous fcc matrix.
The starting alloy has high strength and fatigue performance.
Oxidation kinetics are significant for this alloy over approximately 700–1000 °C.
Chromium diffuses rapidly to the surface under oxidizing conditions.
Surface-enriched chromium forms a protective Cr-rich oxide that limits subsequent oxygen ingress.
Internal Ti-rich oxide precipitates formed in reducing conditions are non-protective and compromise the microstructure.
Oxidizing-atmosphere exposure will cause less mechanical-property degradation than reducing-atmosphere exposure.
Reducing-atmosphere exposure will cause a more rapid decline in fatigue performance relative to the inert baseline.
Under the inert baseline, the homogeneous fcc microstructure is preserved without significant oxidation or internal phase alteration.
Temperatures above the proposed exposure range may prevent the protective scale from retaining its integrity.
